fatal_errors: The proposed boron addition does not reconstruct the target intervention of SPS consolidation at 1000 °C.
None of the cited evidence studies boron additions, boron segregation, or grain-boundary boride films in lightweight high-entropy alloys, so the claimed mechanism lacks cited support.
The falsification rule does not test the full conjunctive claim: failure in one property category can be overlooked if two other measurements improve by more than 10%.
explanation: The hypothesis aligns with the broad application goal by seeking simultaneous mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation improvements at low density, and its modified-versus-unmodified control is reasonable. However, it misses the target material, intervention, processing window, oxide barrier phases, and quantitative outcomes. The target concerns MgAlTiVFeCo powder SPS-sintered at 1000 °C, with comparison against lower-temperature sintering, whereas the generated hypothesis introduces boron into an unspecified alloy. It also omits the critical 800–1000 °C sintering boundary, 900 °C oxidation test, 3.5 wt% NaCl corrosion test, parabolic oxidation kinetics, electrochemical shifts, and target density and hardness values. The proposed boride mechanism is conceivable but speculative; the cited papers concern Cr alloying, selective laser melting, and TiC/Al2O3 reinforcement rather than boron. The experiment is partly discriminating but needs a specified alloy and SPS schedule, replicate statistics, phase and grain-boundary characterization, quantitative electrochemical and oxidation-kinetics criteria, and falsification if any claimed performance dimension fails or density exceeds the limit.
